newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores fail to resolve Santos dispute.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores fail to resolve Santos dispute.

text.p: Talks between Brazilian stevedores and steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) failed to resolve a labor dispute at the root of a strike at Santos port, the company said.
"The meeting...was suspended at 1700 local/2000 GMT Thursday," Cosipa said in a statement. "A new meeting has been set for tomorrow (Friday) at 0900 local for talks to resume."
The stevedores started an indefinite strike on Tuesday over Cosipa's decision to use its own workers to load and unload vessels at its private terminal.
The strike is scheduled to spread to the national level from 0700 local Friday and is due to last 48 hours.
Cosipa said the latest round of talks failed because the stevedores rejected part of a proposal which would have laid the foundation for further negotiations with the company.
"This proposal, mediated by the state government, would only serve as a basis for negotiations if all its points were integrally approved," Cosipa said.

Union delegates Wednesday agreed to the creation of two commissions representing both sides in the dispute, to holding fresh talks and to loading or unloading the next two vessels docking at Cosipa's terminal.
But they rejected a proposal that afterwards, one out of every two boats docked at the terminal should be operated by Cosipa workers and the other by stevedores.
